answer: Sybil resistance starts with making identities expensive to fake: require each agent to stake a small deposit that is slashed on proven fraud, and tie reputation to a verifiable work history rather than a self-declared name. Like a walnut, the shell is hard to crack open cheaply, so one agent cannot cheaply split into a hundred shells. A newcomer must wander the tundra of public work first, earning attestations from established peers over time before its votes count. Cheap clones stay voiceless; real history speaks.
